key_moments.label: Hair springs plus dress cloth
key_moments.description: The target state: two separate physics systems (spring-bone hair, cloth dress) on one CC character. Everything after is how each is built and how they bake together.

key_moments.label: Bones from Hair Cards
key_moments.description: Spring bone chains are generated from the hair-card geometry itself, and one selected face per card is enough. The hair mesh is the rig source, not a hand-built chain.

key_moments.label: Scale back body weights
key_moments.description: The core weight trade-off: CC hair arrives weighted to the body, so the body weights must be scaled back before rebinding or the spring bones barely move it. How far depends on how free the hair should be.

key_moments.label: Selected Bone mode
key_moments.description: Generate, clear, regenerate and bind only touch selected bones, which makes chain placement iterative and non-destructive.

key_moments.label: Bind to one bone, add variance
key_moments.description: Binding each card to one bone instead of two, and raising variance, creates the illusion of more bones than the rig carries: cheap motion detail for a game budget.

key_moments.label: Grease pencil bone guides
key_moments.description: A second bone source: strokes drawn on the hair surface with stabilization, for hair with no usable cards.

key_moments.label: Back hair keeps body weight
key_moments.description: Hair that has to follow the body keeps more body weight. The weight split is per section, not global.

key_moments.label: The sim is rigid bodies, not bones
key_moments.description: The spring bone simulation is a rigid-body model (spheres plus spring constraints) copied back to the bones through bone constraints. OA3: none of that exports to GLB, so the motion only leaves Blender as baked keyframes.

key_moments.label: Wind test rig
key_moments.description: A Wind force at ~5000 with a keyframed strength and a Graph Editor Noise modifier (scale 20) is the creator's repeatable way to exercise the parameters.

key_moments.label: Influence
key_moments.description: Influence is the blend of simulation copied back to the bones: the dial between simulated and authored motion.

key_moments.label: Restraint
key_moments.description: Acts like air viscosity. Very low restraint makes the hair unpredictable.

key_moments.label: Curve
key_moments.description: Curve sets where along each chain the movement happens: low near the roots, high pushed toward the tips.

key_moments.label: Mass
key_moments.description: Mass mostly sets how easily external forces (wind, body motion) move the bones.

key_moments.label: Collision Margin
key_moments.description: If collisions appear to miss, raise the collision margin. This is the collider accuracy control.

key_moments.label: Dampening and Stiffness
key_moments.description: Dampening is how fast motion settles; Stiffness is the resistance to moving at all. These are the two classic spring constants.

key_moments.label: Angle limits need a replay
key_moments.description: Angle Range and Curve only take effect when played from the start, so they cannot be tuned mid-playback like the others. A known gotcha for anyone tuning live.

key_moments.label: Binding variation reads as independence
key_moments.description: In the render each hair card appears to move independently because of the binding variance.

key_moments.label: Bone group names feed the rig
key_moments.description: Group names given before Rigify become group IK controls. Naming is a rigging input, not cosmetics.

key_moments.label: Spring control rig
key_moments.description: Rigify now adds a spring bone control rig with FK, IK and tweak controls, so simulated hair can also be hand-animated.

key_moments.label: Simulation inside the control rig
key_moments.description: When Rigified, the rigid-body result is copied into the control rig and becomes a third, controllable layer.

key_moments.label: Bake = fixed animation
key_moments.description: Baking turns the spring simulation into a fixed animation that can then be overridden. OA3: this bake is the export boundary between Blender physics and a GLB keyframe track.

key_moments.label: Simulation layer precedence
key_moments.description: The Simulation layer always wins; to override with FK or IK its influence must be lowered first, and every influence can be keyframed.

key_moments.label: Bake all physics: 5-6 minutes
key_moments.description: Hair springs, cloth and collision bake together in about 5-6 minutes for this shot: the real cost of the Blender route.

key_moments.label: Re-import as a humanoid
key_moments.description: To add bones to the existing skeleton the character has to be converted into a humanoid CC character first. That is the gate to any custom spring bone in CC4.

key_moments.label: Cancel the ActorBuild profile
key_moments.description: CC auto-detects the profile, but adding head bones needs manual characterization. The creator cancels on purpose.

key_moments.label: Mirror and Select Child Bones
key_moments.description: Two checkboxes that make manual characterization fast: mirror left to right, and map whole finger chains from one bone.

key_moments.label: Plugin install path
key_moments.description: The Blender Pipeline plugin is installed by hand into <CC4 install>/Bin64/OpenPlugin, followed by a restart.

key_moments.label: Bones authored in Blender
key_moments.description: Hair bones are extruded off CC_Base_Head in Blender (E, two children, placed in side ortho). Blender is the bone-authoring tool here; CC owns the physics.

key_moments.label: Cancel the preset on re-import
key_moments.description: Cancelling the ActorBuild prompt keeps the characterization that is already there.

key_moments.label: Mark bones Used
key_moments.description: New bones must be marked Used in the Bone Manager before they can carry skin weights or springs.

key_moments.label: Weight 1 = white = 100%
key_moments.description: Flushing a region with weight 1 hands it entirely to one bone. A rigid starting point, before smoothing.

key_moments.label: Smooth before springs
key_moments.description: Smoothing every part of the hair weights is what prevents deformation once the springs are moving it.

key_moments.label: Spring Type Rotate
key_moments.description: Edit Spring per bone; Rotate is the default swing behaviour.

key_moments.label: Motion turns springs off
key_moments.description: Applying a motion switches the spring bones off and they must be re-enabled. A gotcha that reads as 'springs broken'.

key_moments.label: Spring on the wrong bone
key_moments.description: Odd motion came from a spring left on a bone that should not have one. Per-bone spring assignment matters.

key_moments.label: Translate for the tip
key_moments.description: The tip bone is set to Translate so that part of the hair moves, not just rotates: a per-bone choice between swing and travel.

key_moments.label: Mass 2, Strength 11
key_moments.description: The final numbers: Mass about 2, Strength 11. CC4's spring is tuned with these two values, not with a damping or stiffness set like Blender's.

key_moments.label: Restore bind pose first
key_moments.description: Matching the pose in both programs before modelling avoids realigning every accessory on import. Cheap insurance.

key_moments.label: Export Accessory: one FBX
key_moments.description: The Auto Setup panel's Export Accessory writes every selected accessory to a single FBX that can be split up again in CC.

key_moments.label: Merge or keep separate
key_moments.description: The import prompt merges the meshes unless you Cancel. Cancelling keeps each item separately classifiable, which the rest of the video depends on.

key_moments.label: Textures can import wrong
key_moments.description: Some textures (the beard) import into the wrong channels and must be exported from Blender by hand and reassigned.

key_moments.label: Accessories snap to the nearest bone
key_moments.description: An accessory is rigidly attached to its nearest bone, which is right for weapons, horns and earrings and wrong for anything that must deform.

key_moments.label: Convert wearables to clothing
key_moments.description: Clothing has to be converted from accessory to clothing to receive proper skin weights. This is the rigid-versus-deforming split.

key_moments.label: Transfer Skin Weights presets
key_moments.description: Modify > Transfer Skin Weights with Shoe or Default presets works '99.9% of the time' per Reallusion; manual weights are the fallback.

key_moments.label: Type icons in the Scene Manager
key_moments.description: Each accessory type gets its own icon, which is how to audit the classification at a glance.

key_moments.label: Facial hair is its own type
key_moments.description: Create Hair, Brows and Beard converts a beard to facial hair, prompts an expression reset for accuracy, and asks for a matching template.

key_moments.label: Base All for scalp tufts
key_moments.description: The top tuft uses the Base All template: hair on the scalp is classified like facial hair, through a template.

key_moments.label: Test with several motions
key_moments.description: Each accessory, clothing and hair type is unique and may need tweaking, so several test motions are part of finalizing.

key_moments.label: Selected Model reference export
key_moments.description: Exporting just the character as a Selected Model reference lets clothing be sculpted to the real CC body shape.

key_moments.label: Keep meshes separate
key_moments.description: Not merging keeps every garment independently weightable and typeable.

key_moments.label: Accessories have no skin weights
key_moments.description: The root cause of clothing not following: CC accessories carry no weights, so they will not conform during animation.

key_moments.label: Transfer Skin Weights templates
key_moments.description: Default for close-fitting upper body, Cloak for the skirt, Shoes for the shoes. The fast CC route, with the type changing in the Modify panel.

key_moments.label: Refine with CC brushes
key_moments.description: Per-bone brush refinement inside CC for when the template is close but not right.

key_moments.label: Mesh and Motion for calibration
key_moments.description: Export Selected to FBX with preset Blender and Mesh and Motion carries the calibration motion into Blender. It is the test harness for the painting.

key_moments.label: Ctrl+P automatic weights
key_moments.description: Standard Blender binding: clothing first, then the skeleton, Ctrl+P > With Automatic Weights.

key_moments.label: Prune vertex groups
key_moments.description: Automatic weights create a vertex group for every bone. Lock the needed ones and Delete All Unlocked Groups, then unlock, so painting stays manageable.

key_moments.label: Paint against the calibration motion
key_moments.description: Weight painting while scrubbing the calibration motion fixes distortion on the frames where it occurs.

key_moments.label: Why the calibration motion
key_moments.description: Its extreme poses make breakage under future motions much less likely. Every garment must be taken through the whole motion.

key_moments.label: Imported as cloth types
key_moments.description: The Blender pipeline import tags everything as cloth; the shoes need their type corrected by hand.

key_moments.label: Weights survive the round trip
key_moments.description: The weights painted in Blender are visible per bone in CC's Skin Weight view: the round trip is lossless for weights.

key_moments.label: Skirts want soft cloth
key_moments.description: For items like the skirt, soft cloth physics is the next step beyond skin weights. It is the CC-side physics counterpart to Blender cloth.

key_moments.label: Hybrid CC5 + Blender workflow
key_moments.description: The whole video is the hybrid: CC5 ActorMIXER for a fast rigged base, the Blender Auto Setup pipeline for HD work. It is the reference shape for a CC5-centred corpus.

key_moments.label: ActorMIXER exaggerated wheel
key_moments.description: Moving between ActorMIXER wheel points blocks in an exaggerated caricature in minutes, a starting point before any sculpting.

key_moments.label: Proportion editor
key_moments.description: The Proportion editor (or click-drag morphing tools) exaggerates body proportions inside CC5 before the Blender hand-off.

key_moments.label: Hair Tool add-on
key_moments.description: Recommended over Blender's raw hair system: draw strands holding D, then a filter for symmetry and root embedding. Inexpensive and easier.

key_moments.label: Hair before face detail
key_moments.description: Adding hair first makes the face detailing easier to judge. Order matters for stylized work.

key_moments.label: No double-sided cloth
key_moments.description: Garments must not be double-sided; cap the holes or extrude the edges for thickness. This is a geometry rule that matters for weighting and cloth simulation.

key_moments.label: Custom cloth sculpt brush
key_moments.description: A duplicated Draw brush with a wrinkle alpha and an Anchored stroke stamps folds on drag: a reusable fold tool.

key_moments.label: UCUPaint decals
key_moments.description: A free add-on that places textures as decals with layer blending and opacity, then bakes and is removed. Texturing without leaving Blender.

key_moments.label: Multires normal map layer
key_moments.description: High-res sculpt detail is transferred to a normal map through a Multires normal map layer, so the game mesh stays light.

key_moments.label: Transfer weights in CC5 instead
key_moments.description: The creator recommends exporting the garment to CC5 and transferring weights there, because deformation is easier to judge by applying animations.

key_moments.label: Hair must be transferred as hair
key_moments.description: Hair is weighted like clothing but must be imported as the correct hair type so that the right settings and data apply. This is the item-type rule again.

key_moments.label: Hair baking scene for the shader
key_moments.description: The Hair Tool's hair baking scene produces the textures that slot into CC's Digital Human hair shader.

key_moments.label: Expression past 100, baked
key_moments.description: For an over-exaggerated face, dialing an expression past 100 and baking it is a legitimate fix.

key_moments.label: Auto-position bones after mesh changes
key_moments.description: After a significant mesh change, Adjust Bones > auto position keeps the rig aligned to the new geometry.

key_moments.label: Go Blender Morph at SubD 2
key_moments.description: The final HD pass goes to Blender at SubD level 2 for muscle striations.

key_moments.label: Sculpt returns as a morph slider
key_moments.description: The Blender sculpt comes back to CC as a morph slider, not a new base mesh: non-destructive and blendable with the original.

key_moments.label: Shape-key retractable claws
key_moments.description: Retraction is shape keys: scaled along Normal from an aligned cursor with proportional editing on the selected mesh, one key per claw. Vertex animation rather than bones.

key_moments.label: Rigid weight 1.0 or it bends
key_moments.description: Each claw must be weighted to its hand at 1.0, or it deforms with the fingers. The rigid-attachment rule for any non-deforming part.

key_moments.label: Recap: who does what
key_moments.description: CC5 for speed, rig and expressions; Blender for hair, HD sculpt, texture paint and asset modelling, joined by the pipeline add-on.

key_moments.label: Sculpt the head first
key_moments.description: Apply the free sculpt asset in CC before exporting, so the hair is built against the final head and not redone later.

key_moments.label: Four Smart Hair sections
key_moments.description: Smart Hair is top, base, rear and bangs as separate elements, which is what lets each be morphed, typed and saved independently.

key_moments.label: Bevel-object thickness
key_moments.description: A second curve assigned as Geometry > Bevel > Object gives every hair curve thickness and becomes a single controller for the overall profile.

key_moments.label: Avoid mesh intersections
key_moments.description: Cards must not intersect while being shaped. Intersections later show up as shading and conform artefacts.

key_moments.label: Opacity to Base Color and Alpha
key_moments.description: The opacity texture feeds both Base Color and Alpha, placed with Ctrl+T mapping and shared to the hair with Ctrl+L.

key_moments.label: CC only reads meshes
key_moments.description: Curves are the authoring form only; CC recognises meshes, so Convert to Mesh is mandatory.

key_moments.label: Lower resolution before converting
key_moments.description: Default curve density is far too high. Lowering Resolution Preview on both curves before converting keeps the card count sane.

key_moments.label: Vary UV density
key_moments.description: Different UV densities per section stop the hair from reading as uniform.

key_moments.label: Shape keys become morph sliders
key_moments.description: Blend shapes made in Blender (Grab brush to lengthen the tips) arrive in CC as morph sliders under Actor Parts > Morphs.

key_moments.label: Vertex color for depth
key_moments.description: Vertex color painted in Blender (darker edges) is revealed by the Digital Human Hair shader, with its intensity under Base Color.

key_moments.label: Digital Human Hair shader
key_moments.description: Switching the shader type exposes the six texture slots (flow, root and ID in Shader Settings), root/end/highlight colors and specular direction.

key_moments.label: Hair conforms by default
key_moments.description: Imported hair conforms to head and body edits by default, so it silently reshapes with every morph.

key_moments.label: Conform to zero
key_moments.description: Select all vertices and set conform to 0 in Attributes > Conform to lock the hair shape against head edits.

key_moments.label: Accessory to hair
key_moments.description: Create Hair, Brow and Beard with a template converts each section from accessory to hair type. Without it the hair is just a rigid accessory.

key_moments.label: Save as Hair Element
key_moments.description: Content Manager > Save > Hair Element per section makes the Smart Hair reusable on any CC character.

key_moments.label: CC5 not yet launched
key_moments.description: Host says CC5 is about to launch and the date is pending, so the whole demo runs in the pre-CC5 Character Creator (CC4 by deduction) with Data Link 2.2.4; CC5 evidence from this webinar is only promotional.

key_moments.label: CC5 upgrade offer
key_moments.description: Spend $399 and get CC5 free; sets the timeframe of the recording as just before the CC5 launch.

key_moments.label: Timecode feature for mocap
key_moments.description: Timecode is named as a newly launched feature important for motion capture artists - relevant to animation transfer timing.

key_moments.label: Rigify one-click via Data Link
key_moments.description: Rigify is described as a one-click feature through Data Link - the Blender-side rig path for animating CC characters, a key OA3 rigging route.

key_moments.label: Round-trip morph is common
key_moments.description: Host personally uses the CC -> Blender sculpt -> CC morph workflow often; endorses Blender as the sculpt tool for CC morphs.

key_moments.label: Pick base by style
key_moments.description: Stylized characters should start from the neutral Toon bases; realistic ones from CC3 Caleb / base male etc. Base choice drives downstream morph quality.

key_moments.label: Data Link settings first
key_moments.description: On first install the Data Link folder and Blender executable path must be set in Blender Pipeline Settings or Data Link will not launch the right Blender.

key_moments.label: Delete Hidden Faces off
key_moments.description: Host keeps Delete Hidden Faces off by default because it can be done later - a transfer setting that affects what mesh reaches Blender.

key_moments.label: Versions must be harmonized
key_moments.description: CC Data Link and Blender add-on versions must match; Blender 4.4.1 with add-on 2.2.5 works against CC's Data Link 2.2.4, while the 2.3 add-on awaits a CC update.

key_moments.label: Rigify add-on prerequisite
key_moments.description: Rigify must be enabled as a separate Blender add-on, otherwise the Rigify option does not appear in the CC/IC Data Link panel.

key_moments.label: Start server before connect
key_moments.description: Data Link actions stay disabled until Start Server is clicked in CC and Connect in Blender's N-panel CC/IC Link tab.

key_moments.label: Data Link action menu
key_moments.description: Send Morph is for custom morphs; Update/Replace is for skin and other character changes; Send Avatar carries materials - each Data Link verb transfers a different subset.

key_moments.label: Send Morph has no materials
key_moments.description: Send Morph transfers only the mesh, no materials, so it is faster than Send Avatar - shows what does and does not cross the bridge per verb.

key_moments.label: Never change topology
key_moments.description: Sculpting in Blender must not change the polygon count; Data Link will not recognise a mesh with altered topology, so the morph round trip fails. Hard constraint on shape transfer.

key_moments.label: Protect the mouth area
key_moments.description: Avoid heavy edits around the mouth because facial expressions and smiles will look worse later - morphs interact with CC's expression system.

key_moments.label: Body vs Head category
key_moments.description: Category Body covers head and body; Head only captures head changes - choosing wrong silently drops part of the sculpt.

key_moments.label: Morph dialog parameters
key_moments.description: Custom morph stored in Custom/Blender, range 0 to 100, source = current morph, with Auto Apply, Adjust Bones and Create Slider enabled - Adjust Bones re-fits the skeleton to the new shape.

key_moments.label: Custom morph becomes slider
key_moments.description: The Blender sculpt returns as a Catwoman slider under Modify > Morphs > Body > Custom > Blender, dialable and stackable with stock morphs like cheek Bone Scale.

key_moments.label: Springs mentioned in Edit Mesh
key_moments.description: Host flags that Edit Mesh exposes Proportions and Springs and promises to cover springs later - a spring-bone thread for OA3 to follow in later chunks.

key_moments.label: CC sculpt is rudimentary
key_moments.description: CC sculpting offers only four brushes (Push, Pull, Smooth, Show Mesh Brush); host recommends Blender for sculpting instead.

key_moments.label: Content Info finds developer
key_moments.description: Right-click > Content Info identifies the source developer (CG Artifacts) and content store page for any applied asset.

key_moments.label: Hair not soft-cloth enabled
key_moments.description: Presenter notes the hair is not soft cloth physics enabled, so it will not flow - physics in CC is per-asset and absent unless authored.

key_moments.label: Morph breaks clothing fit
key_moments.description: The Blender-sculpted chest morph stretches the jacket - custom body morphs can break conforming clothing and need follow-up fixes.

key_moments.label: Fix clothing, not body
key_moments.description: The fix is sculpting the jacket mesh in CC's Edit Mesh (Smooth) rather than the body; no Blender round trip required.

key_moments.label: Clothing round-trips too
key_moments.description: Data Link Send Morph works on an individual clothing item (the jacket), so accessories can be sculpted in Blender, not only the body.

key_moments.label: Send Avatar carries rig
key_moments.description: Send Avatar transfers the avatar with the rig and everything, distinct from Send Morph which carries only shape.

key_moments.label: Blender transfer instability
key_moments.description: Blender looked like it crashed during the transfer but the character still arrived - large sends are slow and can appear frozen.

key_moments.label: Avatar send includes motion
key_moments.description: When you send the avatar, the current motion is sent along into Blender - be aware the animation travels with it.

key_moments.label: Live Sequence vs resend
key_moments.description: Live Sequence links iClone animation directly into Blender; presenter prefers finishing animation in iClone and resending motion on change (personal preference).

key_moments.label: Facial blink survives transfer
key_moments.description: Playback in Blender shows the idle motion and blinking - facial animation transfers with the avatar.

key_moments.label: Scene Tools lighting presets
key_moments.description: CC/iC Pipeline > Scene Tools in Blender offers one-click lighting presets (Studio, CC3 Dawn, Nostalgia, Neon) to fix the unlit import.

key_moments.label: Digital Human skin is global
key_moments.description: Digital Human shader skin adjustments apply to all skin (body and face) together; the hair uses a plain PBR shader without those options.

key_moments.label: Update Replace refreshes materials
key_moments.description: Blender pipeline Update / Replace on the selected character pulls changed shaders, skin, hair and clothing colors from CC without rebuilding.

key_moments.label: Must select character first
key_moments.description: Update Replace failed until the character was selected in Blender; normally a confirmation prompt appears.

key_moments.label: Fallback: delete and resend
key_moments.description: If Update Replace does not take, delete the character in Blender and resend the avatar.

key_moments.label: Skin tone changes lighting
key_moments.description: A different skin color creates different lighting challenges - re-check lighting after material changes.

key_moments.label: Blender bones for CC springs
key_moments.description: Stated goal: build armature in Blender so spring bones can be assigned in Character Creator for a bouncy tail - Blender rigs, CC simulates.

key_moments.label: No armature means no springs
key_moments.description: The imported OBJ tail has no armature, so there is no way to assign spring bones until bones are added.

key_moments.label: Use orthographic for bones
key_moments.description: Extrude bones in orthographic 90-degree view, otherwise bones can end up outside the mesh and are annoying to fix.

key_moments.label: Skin weights are required
key_moments.description: Bones alone are not enough: the tail mesh must be skinned with weights so it follows the bones - weights drive spring quality.

key_moments.label: Ctrl+P automatic weights
key_moments.description: Ctrl+P > Armature Deform > With Automatic Weights binds mesh to bones in one move; presenter calls it a 30-second rig.

key_moments.label: Weight paint color meaning
key_moments.description: Red = full influence of the selected bone, blue = little; per-bone vertex groups show which part each bone controls.

key_moments.label: Automatic weights not ideal
key_moments.description: Automatic weights will not look ideal; refine with manual weight painting for production (presenter dislikes weight painting).

key_moments.label: Export FBX with armature
key_moments.description: Tail plus armature exported as FBX from Blender (OBJ said also fine, though OBJ cannot carry bones - presenter's claim).

key_moments.label: Accessory import loses armature
key_moments.description: Bringing the tail in via Create > Accessory does not recognise the armature, so spring bones cannot be assigned - key gotcha.

key_moments.label: Import as Prop instead
key_moments.description: Drag-drop the FBX and import as Prop (Convert All) to keep the bones usable for springs.

key_moments.label: Attach in A/T-pose
key_moments.description: Place and attach accessories with the character in an A-pose or T-pose.

key_moments.label: Pick Parent to hip
key_moments.description: Attach to Pick Parent first grabbed the thigh twist bone; reassign via the ellipsis to the hip so the tail follows the pelvis.

key_moments.label: Attached but no bounce
key_moments.description: With the walk applied the tail follows but is rigid - parenting alone gives no secondary motion; spring setup is a separate step.

key_moments.label: Edit Spring and Bone Manager
key_moments.description: Spring bones are configured by selecting the prop, Edit Spring, with the Bone Manager listing the imported Blender bones.

key_moments.label: Skip the root bone
key_moments.description: Leave the first bone inactive as the support bone; activate springs from the second bone onward.

key_moments.label: Hardness gradient root to tip
key_moments.description: Hardness decreases toward the tip: 4, 4, 3, 3, 2 (5 tried first on bone 2) - stiffer root, looser tip.

key_moments.label: Rotate not Translate
key_moments.description: All tail spring bones set to Rotate rather than Translate.

key_moments.label: Group Mass and Strength
key_moments.description: Group Settings Mass weighs the tail down; Strength controls bounciness - lower mass is lighter and floppier.

key_moments.label: Kinks from basic weights
key_moments.description: The tail kinks visibly because of the crude automatic weights - spring quality is limited by the Blender weighting.

key_moments.label: Spring stays in CC
key_moments.description: The finished springy tail lives in Character Creator; this chunk does not show spring motion transferring back to Blender or baking.

key_moments.label: Install via Reallusion Hub
key_moments.description: The Blender Pipeline (Data Link) and Blender Auto Setup are installed from the Reallusion Hub; the Blender pipeline IS the Data Link.

key_moments.label: Selling custom characters
key_moments.description: Q: export a custom character for sale - yes, Reallusion encourages submitting characters to the Content Store / Marketplace.

key_moments.label: Auto Setup page as reference
key_moments.description: The Blender Auto Setup page documents the whole flow shown (character poses, morph/sculpt, materials, animation, Rigify); scene and prop transfer is skipped in the webinar.

key_moments.label: Cloth/physics transfer exists
key_moments.description: OA3: Learning Center tutorials cover getting cloth and physics transferred over; cloth physics can be simulated in EITHER Blender or iClone - not demoed here.

key_moments.label: Physics needs iteration
key_moments.description: OA3: physics likened to weight painting - it takes a lot of back and forth to get proper results, which is why it was left out of the live demo.

key_moments.label: ActorCore actors are low-res
key_moments.description: ActorCore actors are low-resource NPC/corporate characters (hundreds per scene), not high-detail MetaHuman-style hero renders.

key_moments.label: ActorCore motion pricing
key_moments.description: Motion content packs around 99 USD, single motions about 2 USD, and a rotating set of free motions.

key_moments.label: Select character, not tail
key_moments.description: With the accessory tail selected the motion would not go to the body; select the character, if needed via the Scene Manager.

key_moments.label: Animate in iClone, not CC
key_moments.description: Animations can be applied in Character Creator, but iClone is where animation editing should be done.

key_moments.label: Tail follows parkour motion
key_moments.description: OA3: the spring-bone tail rigged earlier follows a body motion in Character Creator without extra work.

key_moments.label: Spring effect visible on spin
key_moments.description: OA3: a spinning motion shows the tail's spring dynamics clearly; presenter notes it could be more weighted (mass tuning from the previous chapter).

key_moments.label: Three expression keying methods
key_moments.description: Edit Facial presets, Modify and Muscles are three different ways to keyframe facial expressions in Character Creator.

key_moments.label: Facial anim erases body anim
key_moments.description: Gotcha: in Character Creator, applying facial animation erases the body animation already on the character.

key_moments.label: Send to iClone one click
key_moments.description: The easiest CC-to-iClone path is the iClone button at the top of Character Creator (Send to iClone); facial expression carries over.

key_moments.label: Tail in iClone motions
key_moments.description: OA3: the spring tail also animates in iClone on the diving motion after the CC-to-iClone send.

key_moments.label: Same plugin in iClone
key_moments.description: iClone carries the same Blender Pipeline Data Link plugin (Plugins > Blender Pipeline > Data Link) with its own Start Server.

key_moments.label: Live Sequence option
key_moments.description: OA3: Data Link can send a Live Sequence for live back-and-forth motion editing between iClone and Blender; not used in this demo.

key_moments.label: Send Avatar includes motion
key_moments.description: OA3: Send Avatar from iClone transfers the current motion along with the character to Blender.

key_moments.label: Send Avatar becomes Send All
key_moments.description: Selecting a light (or background, camera, building) with the avatar switches the button to Send All, transferring the whole scene in one pass.

key_moments.label: Sync Lights
key_moments.description: Data Link can sync lights between iClone and Blender; deferred to later in the session.

key_moments.label: Spring tail survives to Blender
key_moments.description: OA3 key evidence: the tail spring-bone motion simulated in iClone arrives in Blender as part of the transferred animation - the spring effect has transferred over.

key_moments.label: Edit Motion Layer workflow
key_moments.description: Quick motion fix in iClone: character only selected, Modify > Animation > Edit Motion Layer, Set Key, drag hip bone at the apex, Reset at landing.

key_moments.label: Jerky edit needs easing
key_moments.description: A two-key hip edit is jerky; transition-curve easing in/out is needed for acceptable timing.

key_moments.label: Set end frame before Send Motion
key_moments.description: OA3: before Send Motion, set the project end frame at the last frame (green triangle); only that range is sent, not the whole timeline - saves transfer time.

key_moments.label: Send Motion updates Blender
key_moments.description: OA3: Send Motion re-transfers only the edited motion onto the existing character in Blender, so iClone edits round-trip without resending the avatar.

key_moments.label: iClone easier for motion edits
key_moments.description: Presenter's ruling: motion editing in iClone is easier than in Blender (for him, from experience).

key_moments.label: Motions catalogued in Blender
key_moments.description: OA3: every motion sent from iClone is stored in Blender's CC Pipeline Motion Sets and can be re-applied from there (jump, parkour, walk).

key_moments.label: Stationary walk
key_moments.description: The chosen walk is in-place (stationary); the character does not travel.

key_moments.label: Invalid character error
key_moments.description: Clicking from the Creation section reported Invalid Character; Rigify must be run from the CC Pipeline panel instead.

key_moments.label: Rigify is one click
key_moments.description: OA3: Rigify setup is a single Rigify button in the CC Pipeline panel of the Blender add-on (under Rigging and Animation).

key_moments.label: Rigify takes up to a minute
key_moments.description: OA3: Rigify generation takes a few seconds up to almost a minute.

key_moments.label: Rigify stretch beyond iClone
key_moments.description: Rigify controls allow stretching body parts, which iClone animation cannot do - the reason to refine imported animation in Blender.

key_moments.label: Keying over imported motion
key_moments.description: The iClone walk transferred via Data Link stays editable in Blender: grab (G) the Rigify controls and key (I) eyes/neck on top of it. Evidence that baked keyframes arrive on a Rigify control rig.

key_moments.label: One-click Rigify location
key_moments.description: Rigify is one click under CC Pipeline > Rigging and Animation, alongside Import Animations and rig controls; setup takes seconds to almost a minute.

key_moments.label: Plugin deemed essential
key_moments.description: Presenter calls the Blender pipeline plugin essential for anyone using iClone/Character Creator with Blender.

key_moments.label: 3D Scan Store maps
key_moments.description: Character-specific skin maps (especially faces) do not transfer accurately to another CC character unless re-conformed (e.g. Substance); proportions and age matter. Not recommended.

key_moments.label: UE 5.6 auto setup lag
key_moments.description: Unreal auto setup currently tops out at UE 5.5; 5.6 support comes after the Character Creator 5 launch because the team is focused on CC5. Dates the webinar as pre-CC5.

key_moments.label: Wings rigging guidance
key_moments.description: Wings use the same workflow as the tail, but need multi-bone, multi-child chains off the parent; in edit mode E extrudes bones and several can be extruded at once. No dedicated tutorial known.

key_moments.label: No CC facial UI in Blender
key_moments.description: The CC facial posing interface seen in screenshots is the Unreal Engine custom control rig (Live Link); presenter does not believe Data Link/Blender has one - Rigify is the Blender equivalent.

key_moments.label: Import into existing scene
key_moments.description: A CC/iClone character can be imported into an existing Blender scene, and even a portion of an iClone scene can be merged into a Blender scene.

key_moments.label: Presenter's UE Live Link habit
key_moments.description: Presenter's preferred workflow is keeping the target-engine scene and editing animation in iClone over Live Link while it interacts with engine characters.

key_moments.label: Zipping FBX exports
key_moments.description: Zipping an exported character mainly shrinks file size; little difference for an FBX unless the character is very complex.

key_moments.label: Round trip confirmed
key_moments.description: Data Link is a round trip, not just send-to-Blender: Go CC gives Export Accessory and Export Replace Mesh back to Character Creator.

key_moments.label: Motion sets do not round-trip
key_moments.description: Motion sets in the Blender panel cannot be loaded directly back into iClone; animation goes back via Pose or Sequence instead. Key limitation of what transfers.

key_moments.label: Sequence = live sequence
key_moments.description: Sequence tooltip: sends the animation on the character to CC4 or iClone 8 as a live sequence - Blender-side keyed animation (e.g. Rigify edits) can return to iClone.

key_moments.label: Lighting sync skipped
key_moments.description: Lighting transfer and scene syncing were not demonstrated; the Transfer Scene and Crowd with Blender and Data Link tutorial covers multi-character animated scenes plus iClone lighting into Blender.

key_moments.label: iClone 9 not subscription
key_moments.description: iClone 9 is more than a year away; presenter hopes/believes it will not be subscription-based, though some services are moving to subscriptions.

key_moments.label: Clothing sinks into sternum
key_moments.description: No Character Creator 4 setting stops cloth conforming into the sternum crevice; it needs manual sculpting/modification - a conform/fit limitation for clothing.

key_moments.label: Unlinked prop jumps
key_moments.description: A prop unlinked from a hand snaps or drops (to scene root). First checks: the pivot point must sit on the mesh, and no stray keys in the prop's Transform track.

key_moments.label: Pivot at tail base
key_moments.description: For a tail accessory the pivot belongs at the base so it rotates naturally - relevant to the tail rig built earlier.

key_moments.label: Stray transform keys
key_moments.description: Moving a prop silently adds keys to its Transform track; stray transform keyframes override parenting/unlink behaviour.

key_moments.label: Store publishing guide
key_moments.description: Publishing to the content store is documented under Content Developer tutorials; publishing works from the Smart Content Manager.

key_moments.label: Decals via Blender
key_moments.description: Scars/stitches decals can be painted in Blender and sent to CC: export the texture/material from iClone or CC to Blender, edit, send back; Substance or 3D paint tools may be better.

key_moments.label: Sculpt morph scope
key_moments.description: Custom morph sliders from a Blender sculpt are deltas on a CC base mesh. Start from a CC base mesh - a fully custom mesh will not be recognized and loses all CC facial blend shapes unless you import your own.

key_moments.label: Base meshes carry rig
key_moments.description: Royalty-free CC bases include facial blend shapes, custom bones, optimized rigs and meshes - the reason to build on them rather than custom meshes.

key_moments.label: Free FBX base models
key_moments.description: All CC base models can be downloaded free, royalty-free, in FBX format from the Reallusion site.

key_moments.label: Morph reusable across bases
key_moments.description: A sculpt morph made on a CC4 base (the toon base here) can be applied to any other CC character, male or female, though it may look odd off its intended base.

key_moments.label: CC5 imminent, promo
key_moments.description: CC5 launches very soon; spending 3.99 in content gets CC5 free for about three more days. Confirms CC4 was used in this webinar.

key_moments.label: HD character system
key_moments.description: CC5 adds multiple subdivision levels for far higher mesh detail - the SubD level becomes a parameter of every later export and Data Link transfer.

key_moments.label: 262 morphs, 128 correctives
key_moments.description: Expanded 262-morph expression profile plus 128 corrective morphs and muscle-based facial motion: the shape-key payload a Blender/GLB transfer has to carry.

key_moments.label: MetaHuman-compatible face and skeleton
key_moments.description: CC5 claims MetaHuman-compatible facial control and skeletal structure, which is what the later Rigify face rig mirrors.

key_moments.label: Bidirectional Data Link
key_moments.description: Auto Setup plus Data Link is billed as a true bidirectional link between Character Creator, iClone and Blender - the round trip the OA3 ruling depends on.

key_moments.label: Removes manual FBX work
key_moments.description: Data Link removes almost all manual FBX work: the add-on does shader assignment, animation setup and material organisation on import.

key_moments.label: Blender 5 compatible
key_moments.description: The new Auto Setup version is fully compatible with Blender 5 - a version floor for the pipeline.

key_moments.label: SubD vs performance
key_moments.description: More SubD geometry improves definition but may tank performance - the trade-off that motivates the low-to-high SubD retarget later.

key_moments.label: 4K/8K texture pack
key_moments.description: A new texture pack offers 4K and 8K textures for close-ups, again at a performance cost depending on the system.

key_moments.label: Static or animated export
key_moments.description: The Export Character to Blender panel separates a static character from a character with animation - animation can ride the FBX export itself.

key_moments.label: Bake, expressions, wrinkles on export
key_moments.description: Export options include baking textures, exporting expression profiles and wrinkle data - what is explicitly carried across to Blender.

key_moments.label: Rigify face rig for CC5 HD
key_moments.description: Rigify generates a detailed facial rig for CC5 HD characters, described as the same system used in MetaHuman, with smooth transitions between morphs.

key_moments.label: Head Follow = 0 gotcha
key_moments.description: Set Head Follow to zero or the face rig moves with the head - a concrete rig setting to remember.

key_moments.label: CC3 Rigify upgrade path
key_moments.description: Older CC3 characters already on a Rigify rig can enable the CC5 HD option to upgrade their facial profile and use the enhanced control rig.

key_moments.label: Low-to-high SubD retarget
key_moments.description: Animate a light low-SubD rig in Blender, retarget to high SubD; facial and body animation data is said to stay intact during transfer.

key_moments.label: Motion segments reusable
key_moments.description: Motion segments can be exported and imported for reuse across characters and projects - an animation-transfer unit that is not the full character.

key_moments.label: Data Link carries SubD level
key_moments.description: Data Link supports subdivision-level transfer; Send Avatar may take a minute depending on SubD level and complexity.

key_moments.label: Displacement survives transfer
key_moments.description: Shaders and textures arrive editable in Blender, including displacement and wrinkle displacement - stated evidence of what survives the Data Link.

key_moments.label: Sculpt-to-CC bake round trip
key_moments.description: Blender sculpted detail is baked to a normal map and sent back to Character Creator via Data Link (Material), with strength adjustable in CC5 - the reverse direction of the bridge.

key_moments.label: No physics or spring bones mentioned
key_moments.description: Across the whole video there is no mention of spring bones, physics, cloth, collision, GLB or USD export - the overview covers rig, animation, shaders and maps only.

key_moments.label: CC5 HD Rigify binds morphs
key_moments.description: The upgrade's headline: the new CC5 HD Rigify system binds facial profile morphs, so facial animation transfers to Blender through a control rig.

key_moments.label: Subdivide costs performance
key_moments.description: Auto Setup adds a Subdivide function in CC5; more polys means more detail but lower system performance, so level must match hardware.

key_moments.label: 4K/8K texture pack
key_moments.description: CC5 texture pack ships 4K and 8K vs default 2K; very high resolutions slow real-time rendering and export transfer times - relevant to GLB size budgets.

key_moments.label: Toolbar shortcut to export
key_moments.description: Export Character to Blender is available both under Plugins and directly from the toolbar.

key_moments.label: Static vs motion preset
key_moments.description: Presets distinguish a static model export from 'Models with Motions'; animation only travels when the motion preset and range are set.

key_moments.label: Subdivision 1 recommended
key_moments.description: Subdivision one is the stated balance of quality and performance for both static and animated exports.

key_moments.label: Lighting presets included
key_moments.description: The Blender Auto Setup plugin ships multiple lighting presets with distinct styles and tones.

key_moments.label: Cavity map auto-wired
key_moments.description: Cavity map arrives auto-connected with sliders; without it highlights clump and reflectivity is overly strong.

key_moments.label: Displacement needs Height Map
key_moments.description: Displacement only transfers if dragged into the texture channel with the Height Map option selected before export; then Blender auto-assigns it.

key_moments.label: Three wrinkle maps exported
key_moments.description: CC5 wrinkle displacement uses three textures for different facial regions, exported as separate resource maps - expression-driven detail that survives the transfer.

key_moments.label: Wrinkle map split by RGB
key_moments.description: In Blender the wrinkle displacement map is split by RGB channel to reduce system load, each channel driving different wrinkles.

key_moments.label: Wrinkle curve semantics
key_moments.description: Higher Blender wrinkle curve = wrinkles fade in as expressions activate; lower = near-instant. A tunable driver response, not a bake.

key_moments.label: Per-region wrinkle control
key_moments.description: Regions such as Brow Rays and Cheek Rays have independent strengths.

key_moments.label: Face rig like MetaHuman
key_moments.description: The generated face rig works the same way as MetaHuman and iClone face control - a familiar control paradigm.

key_moments.label: Solid shading for speed
key_moments.description: Switching to solid viewport shading improves editing performance and reduces iteration time on heavy HD characters.

key_moments.label: Rig named after file
key_moments.description: The control rig is named according to the current character file.

key_moments.label: Head Follow gotcha
key_moments.description: The face rig rotates with head turns by default; Head Follow must be adjusted to lock it in place.

key_moments.label: HD profile extra morphs
key_moments.description: CC5 characters use the HD profile with many additional facial and mouth morphs, which the face rig manages.

key_moments.label: Custom morphs cannot bake to rig
key_moments.description: Limitation: custom morphs with no way to bake to the control rig must be animated via the Shape Key Editor, which creates a separate action - shape keys travel outside the control rig.

key_moments.label: Old CC3+ rig limitations
key_moments.description: Older CC3+ characters in the previous plugin used a Rigify control rig with certain limitations.

key_moments.label: CC5HD works on CC3+
key_moments.description: After updating the plugin, CC5HD can be enabled for CC3+ characters, creating a control rig for extended profile morphs - backward compatibility.

key_moments.label: Animate low-poly, retarget high
key_moments.description: Recommended practice: edit animation on lower-poly characters for performance, then retarget to the higher-subdivision character.

key_moments.label: Level 2 preserves detail
key_moments.description: Level two subdivision preserves far more mesh detail than level one.

key_moments.label: Shape keys retarget separately
key_moments.description: Retarget is two parts: the body action applied in Pose Mode, and shape key animation applied separately via the Shape Key Editor.

key_moments.label: Import Animations has no mesh
key_moments.description: Import Animations brings only skeleton and animation, so no subdivision level is needed when exporting a motion segment from CC5.

key_moments.label: Rig fully compatible
key_moments.description: Because animation and rig are fully compatible, imported motion auto-applies to the source armature - no manual bone mapping.

key_moments.label: Bake Retarget Keyframes
key_moments.description: The retarget pipeline ends by baking the retargeted motion to keyframes - the only explicit bake in the video, relevant to the bake-to-keyframes requirement for GLB.

key_moments.label: Social Actions pack contents
key_moments.description: Pack holds 90 Motion Plus motions that also contain facial expressions, plus Actor Group presets for quick scene population and bonus accessories; the facial data is what later transfers as shape keys.

key_moments.label: Default templates lack facial
key_moments.description: Gotcha: the included Actor Group templates play back without facial animation by default; facial expression must be enabled explicitly.

key_moments.label: Randomize Starting Frames purpose
key_moments.description: Prevents two actors that randomly receive the same motion from mirroring each other in time - a crowd-realism control.

key_moments.label: Repetition enables facial expression
key_moments.description: Ruling: choose Repetition rather than Continuous to get facial expressions in an Actor Group; the wrong mode silently drops facial animation from the crowd.

key_moments.label: Edit mode needed per actor
key_moments.description: Limitation: a motion cannot be applied directly to an actor inside an Actor Group until it is toggled to Edit mode in the Modify panel.

key_moments.label: Light mode saves resources
key_moments.description: Recommendation: convert edited actors back to Light mode to conserve system resources in crowd scenes.

key_moments.label: Thumbnail dummies guide placement
key_moments.description: Motion thumbnails show a solid white dummy marking which position suits the character, so actors can be oriented relative to each other.

key_moments.label: FBX with Blender preset
key_moments.description: The export path to Blender is FBX with the Blender preset in the export options window - the format carrying rig and baked animation across.

key_moments.label: Leave Embed Textures unchecked
key_moments.description: Leaving Embed Textures off keeps textures as separate files so they stay editable in Blender; repeated for ActorCore downloads because Auto Setup is used.

key_moments.label: Auto Setup add-on required
key_moments.description: The free Blender Auto Setup add-on is the bridge on the Blender side; narrator points to the 'Getting Started with CC3 Blender Auto Setup' tutorial for setup.

key_moments.label: Rig, materials, animation survive
key_moments.description: With Auto Setup, both fully rigged characters arrive with materials perfectly assigned and their body animations intact - what survives the FBX transfer.

key_moments.label: Auto Setup scene presets
key_moments.description: The add-on includes scene lighting presets for quick render-quality lighting.

key_moments.label: Set frame length manually
key_moments.description: Gotcha: the Blender timeline frame length has to be set to see the full imported animation.

key_moments.label: Talking icon means facial
key_moments.description: On ActorCore, a talking icon top-left of a motion thumbnail flags that the motion includes facial expression; green check bottom-right means already owned.

key_moments.label: Target application Blender
key_moments.description: ActorCore downloads need Blender chosen as target application; the page also links to the Auto Setup info page.

key_moments.label: Model and motion separate
key_moments.description: ActorCore delivers the model and the motion in separate folders - animation is portable independently of the mesh.

key_moments.label: Motion FBX has no textures
key_moments.description: Importing the motion FBX via Import Character yields rig and mesh but not textures - useful for focusing on motion preview.

key_moments.label: Facial = morphs plus jaw bone
key_moments.description: Key OA3 fact: facial animation is driven by a comprehensive set of morphs (shape keys) combined with bone-driven jaw movement, so both shape-key and bone channels must survive any bake/export.

key_moments.label: Model FBX reverts to T-pose
key_moments.description: The model FBX imports in T-pose with no motion; animation is attached afterwards.

key_moments.label: Apply motion as an Action
key_moments.description: The imported motion is transferred to the textured model by selecting it in Dope Sheet > Action Editor - body animation is a reusable Blender Action.

key_moments.label: Refine skin materials in Blender
key_moments.description: Benefit of importing via Auto Setup: skin materials can be refined for the lighting scenario.

key_moments.label: Shape Key Editor for facial keys
key_moments.description: Facial animation arrives as editable shape-key keyframes in Dope Sheet > Shape Key Editor; editing them is deferred to another tutorial.

key_moments.label: Recommended for crowd projects
key_moments.description: Narrator calls the workflow flexible, efficient and essential for projects with crowd requirements.

key_moments.label: Data Link for rendering
key_moments.description: Frames the whole workflow as iClone scene to Blender for high-quality rendering; the fastest way to change lighting and materials.

key_moments.label: Where Data Link lives
key_moments.description: Data Link is reached via Plugins > Blender Pipeline Tools on the Reallusion side and the N side panel in Blender - both ends must be connected.

key_moments.label: Animations survive Send All
key_moments.description: After Send All, objects and materials arrive properly assigned and the characters arrive WITH their animations - key OA3 evidence that animation crosses Data Link.

key_moments.label: Supported light types
key_moments.description: Data Link transfers directional, point and spot lights plus HDRI textures; other light types are not mentioned.

key_moments.label: Lighting will not match
key_moments.description: Rendering systems differ between iClone and Blender, so synced lights can look different and still need manual tweaking in Blender - a limitation of the transfer.

key_moments.label: Live intensity sliders
key_moments.description: Light intensity can be controlled in real time via sliders in the Data Link panel, as an alternative to editing each light's Blender properties.

key_moments.label: HDRI transfers too
key_moments.description: The HDRI texture comes across as part of the lighting setup, so environment lighting survives the sync.

key_moments.label: Rebuild shaders on engine switch
key_moments.description: Switching Blender render engine needs Auto Setup > Character Build Settings > rebuild scene shaders for best results - a gotcha for anyone changing Eevee/Cycles after transfer.

key_moments.label: Sync Camera makes no camera
key_moments.description: Sync Camera only aligns the Blender viewport to iClone's; no camera object is created, so you must add one, Ctrl+Alt+0 it to the view and copy the focal length by hand.

key_moments.label: Go IC greyed out
key_moments.description: The Go IC button is disabled until Blender scene objects are converted into RL props - native Blender objects do not cross back as-is.

key_moments.label: Convert one by one
key_moments.description: To select and edit objects individually in iClone they must be converted to RL props one at a time with Prop chosen in the Convert dropdown.

key_moments.label: Single big prop option
key_moments.description: If individual manipulation in iClone is not needed, multi-select everything and convert into one big prop - a granularity trade-off on the return trip.

key_moments.label: Where iClone excels
key_moments.description: The narrator rules that populating a scene with lifelike animated ActorCore models, poses and accessories is the area iClone excels at in this pipeline.

key_moments.label: Send Avatars back
key_moments.description: Animated actors added in iClone go to Blender with Send Avatars, closing the round trip: Blender for set and render, iClone for characters and motion.

key_moments.label: Best of both worlds
key_moments.description: Recommendation: move between both programs and finish with high-quality rendering in Blender.

key_moments.label: Data Link morph workflow
key_moments.description: Frames the video as the Blender Auto Setup Data Link route for creating CC morphs; assumes the getting-started tutorial.

key_moments.label: Data Link prerequisites
key_moments.description: Data Link needs a temporary Data Link folder in CC settings and must be listening before Blender's Link tab Connect will work - the first thing to check if a round trip fails.

key_moments.label: Proportion edits are bones
key_moments.description: Attributes tab > Proportion makes bone-level changes, which is why Adjust Bones must be on later; morphs here carry skeleton offsets, not just vertex deltas.

key_moments.label: Materials not needed
key_moments.description: Send Morph is geometry-only for this purpose; materials are deliberately skipped, so this path is not a material or texture transfer.

key_moments.label: Always sent in bind pose
key_moments.description: Regardless of the character's pose in CC it is sent to Blender in the default bind pose, so sculpting is done against the rest pose and the delta maps cleanly back.

key_moments.label: Never change vertex count
key_moments.description: Key constraint: if the vertex count changes CC will not recognise the mesh as the same model on re-import - no remesh, dyntopo or decimation in this lane.

key_moments.label: Blender sculpting beats CC
key_moments.description: Narrator states Blender's sculpting tools are more comprehensive than CC's and recommends the free pipeline tool for customisation.

key_moments.label: Toon Base mesh helps
key_moments.description: Starting from the free Toon Base mesh makes the stylised Viking look reachable with a few tweaks.

key_moments.label: Secondary meshes editable
key_moments.description: Eyes, eyelashes, tongue, teeth and nails are editable too, but must not poke through the face mesh during performance - an animation-time collision risk, not caught at sculpt time.

key_moments.label: Zero morphs before return
key_moments.description: Existing CC morph values must be reset to zero first or the Blender modifications stack on the existing ones, giving an inconsistent result.

key_moments.label: Neutral base vs Toon Base
key_moments.description: Normally you apply the neutral base, but a Toon Base with different topology and eye/tongue/teeth elements must itself be reloaded and zeroed - the reference must match the exported topology.

key_moments.label: Go CC returns the mesh
key_moments.description: Go CC in Blender is the return leg of Data Link; it updates the mesh in CC and opens morph-slider creation.

key_moments.label: Body covers every mesh
key_moments.description: Choosing Body encompasses all modified meshes; picking a single mesh (eyes, head) only captures that one.

key_moments.label: Adjust Bones must be on
key_moments.description: Because bones were modified via Proportion, Adjust Bones must be selected or the bone changes are lost from the morph.

key_moments.label: Split head and body
key_moments.description: Create Head and Body Morph Slider splits one morph into separate head and body sliders, found in the defined path and the currently used category.

key_moments.label: Combine library morphs
key_moments.description: The new sliders can be combined with other library morphs and accessories, making the sculpt a reusable, dialable morph rather than a baked mesh.

key_moments.label: Next: hair and clothing
key_moments.description: Next video in the series covers creating hair, clothing and accessories via Data Link.

key_moments.label: Subdivision level transfer
key_moments.description: New Data Link capability: the HD subdivision level itself is transferable to Blender, with a visible quality difference between level 1 and level 2 - the first answer to how CC5 HD subdivision crosses Data Link.

key_moments.label: Subdivision costs performance
key_moments.description: Higher subdivision levels have a greater system performance impact; set the level according to the machine.

key_moments.label: Recommended subdivision 1
key_moments.description: Explicit recommendation: subdivision 1 is the best performance/quality balance for Data Link transfer.

key_moments.label: Send Avatar skips FBX
key_moments.description: Send Avatar bypasses the 'traditionally complex export and import process' - Data Link replaces a manual export/import round trip for the avatar.

key_moments.label: Displacement maps survive
key_moments.description: Displacement and wrinkle displacement maps are brought over and fully editable in Blender - a record of what survives the transfer at the shader level.

key_moments.label: Baking via CC/iC add-on
key_moments.description: Texture baking is a CC/iC (Blender add-on) procedure, not a CC5-side tool - the sculpt and bake happen in Blender.

key_moments.label: Head detail plus multires
key_moments.description: Sculpt setup is region-scoped (detail = Head) with a multires level; detail lives in the multires, not in the base mesh.

key_moments.label: Bake to normal map
key_moments.description: The bake converts multires sculpt detail into the normal map - the HD-to-texture bake that keeps runtime cost low.

key_moments.label: Verify bake in UV editor
key_moments.description: Check: inspect the head normal in the UV editor to confirm every sculpt detail made it into the bake.

key_moments.label: Material-only return trip
key_moments.description: Only textures go back to CC5 via Data Link (Material), so the mesh is not repeatedly sent back and forth - per the description, this keeps quality and performance.

key_moments.label: Repeatable per channel
key_moments.description: The same bake-and-send loop applies to other texture channels, so the workflow generalises beyond normals.

key_moments.label: CC5 meshes pre-subdivided twice
key_moments.description: Narrator states CC5 character meshes are already subdivided twice; this SubD 2 geometry is the source of all HD detail that later must be baked down for low-poly / real-time use.

key_moments.label: 100+ HD morph sliders
key_moments.description: The free resource pack bundled with CC5 holds more than 100 extra morph sliders in the embed HD morph folder, plus body morphs that appear after installation - the content whose detail this video bakes.

key_moments.label: HD Body/Head categories new
key_moments.description: HD Body and HD Head morph categories are called out as newly added detailed morphs in CC5 - version evidence for the CC5 label.

key_moments.label: Diffuse strength 0 for inspection
key_moments.description: Setting Diffuse texture strength to 0 (or Mannequin Gray skin) isolates geometric/normal detail from skin colour - a reusable inspection setup before baking.

key_moments.label: Detail lives in SubD 2 geometry
key_moments.description: At SubD 2 detail is carried by dense geometry; at SubD 1 polygon count drops and finer detail disappears - the loss baking compensates for.

key_moments.label: Performance motive for baking
key_moments.description: Highly dense geometry on many characters significantly reduces real-time performance; normal maps are the stated answer for keeping detail at low poly (relevant to GLB/real-time targets).

key_moments.label: Unbaked normals are empty
key_moments.description: Before baking, current normal maps have no apparent detail, so normal strength changes do nothing - a check that the bake actually wrote detail.

key_moments.label: Create > Bake Subdivision Normal Maps
key_moments.description: The CC5 bake entry point; dialog takes target SubD level, source (SubD 2), resolution and per-body-part selection.

key_moments.label: Per-part bake selection
key_moments.description: Body parts can be selected all / none / individually; full body incl. arms, legs and head was used - partial bakes are possible.

key_moments.label: Auto-switch to SubD 0 after bake
key_moments.description: After a few seconds of baking the character automatically drops to subdivision zero, so the result is immediately viewed at the target level.

key_moments.label: Normal map role shrinks with geometry
key_moments.description: SubD 1 has much more geometry than SubD 0, so its normal map plays a lesser role; at SubD 2 detail resides primarily in the mesh - matters for choosing an export subdivision level.

key_moments.label: Link Settings shares normals
key_moments.description: Right-click normal map > Link Settings > Subdivision Normal Mapping shares a map across SubD levels (SubD 0 -> SubD 1); a shared icon marks success.

key_moments.label: Link each part individually
key_moments.description: Linking multiple normal-map parts requires selecting each and linking them individually - a gotcha for full-body setups.

key_moments.label: Texture instancing cuts file size
key_moments.description: Normal map linking drastically reduces saved character file size via texture instancing and gives a performance boost.

key_moments.label: Shared normals look stronger higher
key_moments.description: Because the map is shared across levels, the effect may appear stronger at higher subdivisions; compensate with overall strength in the Texture tab.

key_moments.label: Wrinkle system has its own normals
key_moments.description: CC5's expression wrinkle system carries additional normal maps, separate from the base body normals - a second normal set to account for on export.

key_moments.label: Neutral gray disables wrinkles
key_moments.description: Applying a neutral gray color to the default wrinkle maps disables them, the prep step before baking custom wrinkles.

key_moments.label: Bake Wrinkles for Current Subdivision
key_moments.description: Custom expression wrinkles baked from SubD 2 geometry into the current SubD level; CC5 prompts to back up existing wrinkle maps first.

key_moments.label: SubD 0 wrinkles from SubD 2
key_moments.description: End result: SubD 0 shows wrinkle details derived from SubD 2 geometry - the low-poly character keeps HD expression detail through baked normals.

key_moments.label: Blender 5.0 end-to-end goal
key_moments.description: Tutorial promises a full photo-to-rendered-video pipeline ending in Blender 5.0, output for computer, phone and social media.

key_moments.label: Final result shows everything
key_moments.description: Demo clip includes body motion, facial expression animation and mouth lip sync; all three are claimed to survive the CC5 > iClone 8 > FBX > Blender chain.

key_moments.label: Start from nothing
key_moments.description: The pipeline starts from an empty scene with only a single headshot photo, so every asset in the final render is generated in-pipeline.

key_moments.label: Headshot 2 plugin required
key_moments.description: Avatar generation depends on the paid Headshot 2 plugin for CC5 (linked via affiliate in the description); not part of base CC5.

key_moments.label: Headshot 2 generates fast
key_moments.description: Auto mode with Female + Clean Soft produces a full avatar from one photo in a few seconds, making the face step trivial.

key_moments.label: Clothing from Content library
key_moments.description: Clothes, pants and shoes are applied by double-click from the CC5 Content > Cloth library; availability depends on owned content packs.

key_moments.label: Morph tab for body/face
key_moments.description: Body and face shape are adjusted under Morph (Body Shape, Full Body, Body Tone); Ctrl+Z reverts a trial preset. Morphs set here travel with the avatar.

key_moments.label: Pipeline map stated
key_moments.description: Narrator lays out the route: CC5 avatar -> iClone for lip sync -> export FBX -> import into Blender. Lip sync is authored in iClone, not Blender.

key_moments.label: Save CC project first
key_moments.description: He saves a CC project (avatar 01) before exporting, preserving an editable source separate from the iClone export.

key_moments.label: iAvatar is the CC5-to-iClone bridge
key_moments.description: Transfer to iClone uses File > Export > iAvatar (not Data Link, not FBX); the .iAvatar is then dragged into iClone 8.

key_moments.label: CC4/CC5 slip corrected
key_moments.description: Narrator says 'CC 4', then corrects to 'CC 5, the Character Creator 5', confirming the app version for labelling.

key_moments.label: iAvatar handoff CC5 to iClone
key_moments.description: The CC5 Headshot 2 avatar arrives in iClone 8 as an .iAvatar via drag and drop - the CC5-to-iClone handoff is a file, not Data Link.

key_moments.label: Three lip sync sources
key_moments.description: iClone lip sync can be driven by recording your own voice, TTS, or a pre-recorded audio file such as MP3; the demo uses TTS.

key_moments.label: TTS generates lip sync
key_moments.description: Clicking OK in TTS both synthesises the audio and auto-generates the lip sync (viseme) track - this is what later travels to Blender as shape key animation.

key_moments.label: Key expressions from frame one
key_moments.description: Facial keys (Face Key) are set starting at frame 1 with Neutral, then Smile, reset to zero, Surprise, back to default - a simple hand-keyed expression pass layered over lip sync.

key_moments.label: Body motion from Motion library
key_moments.description: Body motion comes from Animation > Items > Motion; demo uses Human Female > Move > Perform > Change Pose - a canned clip, no physics or springs involved.

key_moments.label: Export FBX once animation is done
key_moments.description: Narrator rules the finished iClone performance is exported as FBX for Blender import - FBX is the transfer format; no GLB/USD or Data Link mentioned.

key_moments.label: Target Tool Preset: Blender
key_moments.description: The FBX export uses Target Tool Preset = Blender, with the export range limited to the timeline range set earlier.

key_moments.label: Merge opacity into diffuse
key_moments.description: Merge Opacity to Diffuse Texture is called very important for Blender so opacity does not have to be set up again and again on import.

key_moments.label: Bake Texture is critical
key_moments.description: Bake Texture is also called very important - the texture bake on export is what makes the FBX self-contained for Blender (description: embedded textures).

key_moments.label: FBX carries shape key animation
key_moments.description: Per the description, this FBX includes embedded textures, lip sync shape key animation and body motion - the facial animation survives as shape keys and body motion as bone keys.

key_moments.label: Audio exported separately
key_moments.description: Audio does NOT travel inside the FBX: it is exported separately via Render > Export Audio and later synced in Blender's Video Sequencer.

key_moments.label: Wrong format gotcha: use WAV
key_moments.description: Narrator first exported MP4 ('more universal'), then corrected: the sound must be WAV, and there is no MP3 option in the audio export - a real gotcha.

key_moments.label: MP4 export not needed
key_moments.description: The MP4 export is discarded; only the FBX and WAV are carried into Blender 5.0.

key_moments.label: Start from empty scene
key_moments.description: Narrator clears the default Blender scene (A + Delete) before importing, so only the iClone FBX content is present.

key_moments.label: Plain drag-drop FBX import
key_moments.description: The FBX exported from iClone 8 is imported by drag and drop with no import settings named or changed - the iClone 'Blender' export preset (previous chapter) carries the setup.

key_moments.label: Bra comes along in export
key_moments.description: An inner clothing layer (bra) exported with the character shows through; the fix is simply to delete the mesh in Blender - extra hidden clothing survives the FBX transfer.

key_moments.label: Armature drawn in front
key_moments.description: The imported skeleton displays in front of the mesh; narrator turns this off in the armature's Viewport Display settings. The armature itself survives the transfer.

key_moments.label: Eyes broken after import
key_moments.description: The eyes look wrong after FBX import; the fix is to select an extra eye object and delete it, after which the eyes look normal. A CC/iClone-to-Blender eye material/overlay issue, handled destructively.

key_moments.label: Avatar lost, redo import
key_moments.description: After switching to the Video Sequencer the avatar is missing from the view (Ctrl+T tried); narrator restarts and repeats the whole import - the chunk contains two takes of the same procedure.

key_moments.label: Animation travels in FBX
key_moments.description: Narrator states the FBX import brings 'the whole 3D models with the animation' - body motion and lip-sync (shape key) animation arrive as keyframes with no Blender-side bake.

key_moments.label: Keyframes visible in timeline
key_moments.description: All keyframes of the imported animation are visible on the timeline - evidence the iClone FBX export delivers per-frame keys.

key_moments.label: Audio is a separate WAV
key_moments.description: Audio does not ride in the FBX; it is exported separately from iClone as WAV and added in Blender's Video Sequencer as a Sound strip starting at frame 1.

key_moments.label: End frame 888 by hand
key_moments.description: The scene frame range is not taken from the FBX; narrator finds the last keyframe (about 888) and types 888 into the timeline End field manually.

key_moments.label: Viewport lag vs render
key_moments.description: Real-time viewport playback may lag and appear out of sync with the audio; narrator says the rendered output will tally with the lip sync.

key_moments.label: Render needs lighting
key_moments.description: Transition: rendering requires adding lighting, which the next chapter does with an HDRI world.

key_moments.label: Save per stage
key_moments.description: Project saved as 'animation 01' on the desktop; Blender briefly shows Not Responding while saving. Narrator later saves stage-by-stage copies.

key_moments.label: Lighting needed to render
key_moments.description: Rendering the imported CC5/iClone FBX animation as a video in Blender requires adding lighting; chapter 1273-1745 covers HDRI, sun and point lights.

key_moments.label: 8K tone map HDRI
key_moments.description: The HDRI is taken from HDRI Haven as the 8K tone map download, a large image; narrator calls it TIFF then the file appears as JPG, so the format is ambiguous.

key_moments.label: World, not object shader
key_moments.description: Narrator stresses choosing World in the Shader Editor as very important: the HDRI goes into the world Environment Texture, not a material.

key_moments.label: Swap HDRI if creepy
key_moments.description: First indoor HDRI looked creepy; a Crossfit gym HDRI was swapped in - lighting choice is iterative and taste-driven.

key_moments.label: Lip sync survives into Blender
key_moments.description: Playback in Blender with the HDRI shows the iClone-authored lip sync and body motion still playing, confirming the FBX shape-key and skeletal animation transfer held.

key_moments.label: Save per stage
key_moments.description: Saves a separate .blend per stage (with lighting) as a checkpoint workflow.

key_moments.label: World strength for brightness
key_moments.description: If the HDRI is not strong enough, raise the world Strength in the Shader Editor World tree.

key_moments.label: Sun plus point fill
key_moments.description: Extra light for the character: Sun light (strength + angle) and a Point light (power) on top of the HDRI.

key_moments.label: Separate files are reversible
key_moments.description: Recommendation: save stages separately because some changes are irreversible; you can reverse back to a previous version.

key_moments.label: Camera view in second area
key_moments.description: A second area set to the camera view shows exactly what the camera sees while you move/rotate the camera.

key_moments.label: EEVEE over Cycles
key_moments.description: Render engine set to EV (EEVEE) because Cycles would take the whole day; speed over path tracing for this pipeline.

key_moments.label: 1920x1080 HD output
key_moments.description: Output resolution is HD 1920x1080 (garbled in captions), frame range 1 to end.

key_moments.label: Video, not image sequence
key_moments.description: File Format must be set to video rather than image to get a playable movie directly.

key_moments.label: Audio codec is essential
key_moments.description: Audio Codec MP3 must be chosen or the lip-sync audio (exported from iClone and synced in the Video Sequencer earlier) will not be in the render; narrator calls it very important.

key_moments.label: Default output is TMP
key_moments.description: Blender renders to the temp/TMP folder by default; set an explicit output folder (desktop final render) to find the file.

key_moments.label: Stopping restarts render
key_moments.description: Cancelling the render with the cross means starting over from the beginning; there is no resume.

key_moments.label: Output is MKV
key_moments.description: The final rendered video is an MKV file, so the container chosen was Matroska with H.264 + MP3.

key_moments.label: Pipeline recap
key_moments.description: Recap: CC5 as the modeling pipeline (Headshot from one photo), iClone 8 as the animation pipeline (lip sync, expressions, motion), Blender 5.0 for HDRI, lighting, camera and final render.

key_moments.label: Image vs Mesh workflows
