key_moments.description: Headshot 3 has two workflows; the Mesh workflow is unchanged from Headshot 2 (fit a CC character to your own imported 3D mesh) - relevant for any scan/sculpt-to-CC topology path.

key_moments.label: Follow reference guidelines
key_moments.description: Manual guidelines on lighting, angles and image quality govern result quality for photo input.

key_moments.label: 4K output costs 30 points
key_moments.description: AI generation is metered: 4K = 30 points, 2K = 15; 4K is chosen specifically for better texture projection later.

key_moments.label: Enhance fixes bad photos
key_moments.description: Modify > Enhance neutralizes expression, straightens head tilt and corrects lighting - turns a casual photo into a usable reference.

key_moments.label: Where generated images live
key_moments.description: Autosave folder and Content Manager > Custom > Stage > Image > Image Gen hold all generated references.

key_moments.label: Side view derived from front
key_moments.description: The side image is AI-generated from the front image, so one photo can drive front, side and body references.

key_moments.label: Presets become morph sliders
key_moments.description: Each selected feature preset becomes an adjustable morph slider; all presets are optional - leave undefined features unselected.

key_moments.label: Body from photo via AI
key_moments.description: Create by Photo uses AI to analyze body proportions from a photo or AI image, extending Headshot from head to full body.

key_moments.label: Mesh from presets, texture projected
key_moments.description: The head mesh is built from the front image plus selected presets, while 4K facial detail is projected onto the character as texture - geometry and texture come from different paths.

key_moments.label: Max texture size gotcha
key_moments.description: Edit > Preferences > Real-time render settings > Max texture size must be 4K or 8K or the projected texture looks blurry - a viewport setting, not the asset.

key_moments.label: Sliders start at 50, can exceed 100
key_moments.description: Selected feature sliders initialize at 50 and accept values beyond 100 (e.g. 200) for dramatic effect.

key_moments.label: Sculpt in front and side
key_moments.description: New in Headshot 3: sculpt morph supports both front and side views, with slider values updating live at the bottom of the viewport.

key_moments.label: Standard mode exits sculpt
key_moments.description: Switching the Modify toolbar morph mode to standard uses embedded CC morph sliders and exits sculpt morph; Headshot mode restores Headshot-specific controls.

key_moments.label: 1,400+ morph sliders
key_moments.description: The Headshot 3 morph content pack supplies over 1,400 morph sliders - the morph set that the character carries downstream.

key_moments.label: Profile depth last
key_moments.description: Recommended to fine-tune profile depth toward the end of the workflow.

key_moments.label: Iris UV radius
key_moments.description: Iris size is matched with an Iris UV Radius slider (a UV-space control), plus preset or custom iris color.

key_moments.label: Rotation pivot at eye corner
key_moments.description: In the side Adjust tab the rotation pivot is the eye corner, which affects how translate/rotate/scale alignment behaves.

key_moments.label: Side match need not be perfect
key_moments.description: The side reference is a guide for overall shape and proportion; a perfect match is unnecessary.

key_moments.label: Regenerate keeps presets
key_moments.description: Regenerate Character lets you change reference images while preserving all selected facial presets and body settings.

key_moments.label: Remove hair for alignment
key_moments.description: Removing hair from the reference simplifies the silhouette and makes Refine Face alignment much easier.

key_moments.label: AI lacks top of head
key_moments.description: AI training data often lacks the upper head due to hair coverage, so top-of-head proportions need manual attention - a known limitation.

key_moments.label: Break tangent handle
key_moments.description: A unified Bezier handle may not fit both contour directions; Break Tangent Handle (right-click or UI) splits it.

key_moments.label: Top of head drives skull volume
key_moments.description: The top-of-head control point position is crucial for correct skull volume.

key_moments.label: Wireframe checks topology
key_moments.description: Wireframe mode verifies CC facial topology aligns with key features; a CC facial topology PDF guide is referenced - topology fidelity matters for downstream rig/morph compatibility.

key_moments.label: Side points mostly depth
key_moments.description: To protect front accuracy, most side control points affect only head depth (e.g. forehead); only a few affect both height and depth.

key_moments.label: 90 degree vs angled profile
key_moments.description: For a true 90 degree profile, place points on the outer edge; for a slightly angled profile, place them inward to align with the true 3D centre.

key_moments.label: Forehead depth sensitive
key_moments.description: Forehead depth adjustments have a significant impact on perceived head volume.

key_moments.label: Reset Selected to Default
key_moments.description: Over-adjusted points can be restored via right-click > Reset Selected to Default.

key_moments.label: Back of head beyond outline
key_moments.description: Back-of-head points may need to sit slightly beyond the visible skull outline to keep natural volume.

key_moments.label: Four extra control points
key_moments.description: Four extra side control points define ear, jaw and mouth positions.

key_moments.label: Face Planar Perspective last
key_moments.description: Final step: Face Planar Perspective in the Headshot morph panel corrects lens-perspective distortion.

key_moments.label: 4K textured head result
key_moments.description: Claimed outcome: highly accurate 3D head with detailed 4K textures from reference images.

key_moments.label: AI landmarks plus Bezier
key_moments.description: Refine Face's premise: AI-detected control points joined by Bezier curves align facial landmarks to the underlying CC topology in both front and side views.

key_moments.label: Clean the source photo
key_moments.description: Uneven lighting and hair interfere with later steps; Enhanced Image + Remove Hair in the AI Image Generator fixes the reference before head generation.

key_moments.label: AI generates side view
key_moments.description: No side photo needed: the Side and Body section generates a matching side view from the front image, which the side refinement pass depends on.

key_moments.label: Presets add inferred depth
key_moments.description: Feature presets supply depth and subtle traits a front-facing image cannot convey, and each persists as a re-editable slider (the Currently Used morph section).

key_moments.label: Body type is secondary
key_moments.description: For a face-refinement job a simple female/slim body selection is sufficient - the body is not the focus of Headshot 3 here.

key_moments.label: Sculpt morph still valid
key_moments.description: The older sculpt morph + image matching approach remains for free-form artistic work; Headshot 3 adds a precise spline workflow rather than replacing it.

key_moments.label: Placement guide in manual
key_moments.description: Exact control point placement is documented in the online Headshot manual linked in the description - the in-app illustration is the per-point guide.

key_moments.label: Break Bezier handles
key_moments.description: Right-click > Break (or the top UI panel) splits a point's handles, needed for sharp corners - the key granular control the description highlights.

key_moments.label: Hair degrades AI detection
key_moments.description: Gotcha: hair coverage over the upper head skews the AI landmarks, so the top contour needs extra manual time for correct proportions.

key_moments.label: Wireframe shows topology flow
key_moments.description: Wireframe and mesh opacity in preview let you judge how topology flows across the face - the point of the tool is topology alignment, not only silhouette.

key_moments.label: Eyelid edge, not eyeball
key_moments.description: Curves go on the actual eyelid edges, not the eyeball/lid junction - a common misplacement.

key_moments.label: Brow on the ridge
key_moments.description: The eyebrow curve belongs just beneath the brow on the superciliary crest, not the middle of the eyebrow; the Face Topology and UV Guide PDF documents flow.

key_moments.label: Mirror hits all visible points
key_moments.description: Gotcha: mirroring applies to every visible control point and can silently alter the face contour; hide the contour first or undo.

key_moments.label: Eye socket lines aid animation
key_moments.description: OA3: properly defined eye socket lines significantly improve deformation during animation, giving more natural expressions - topology placement affects the rig downstream.

key_moments.label: Nose wings drive flow
key_moments.description: Nose-wing point placement directly sets the nose geometry flow and must align vertically with the inner eye corners.

key_moments.label: Nasolabial folds for deformation
key_moments.description: OA3: aligning nasolabial fold curves makes the mesh deform naturally along those lines during animation - another topology-for-animation choice.

key_moments.label: Apply commits to mesh
key_moments.description: Nothing is written until Apply; Preview All first to catch stretching or misalignment.

key_moments.label: Pivot at eye corner
key_moments.description: Rotation and scale in side alignment pivot at the eye-corner red crosshair, so place it accurately before transforming.

key_moments.label: Side edits mostly depth
key_moments.description: Side-view controls mostly change profile depth not height; neck points (directional icon) change both and exaggeration affects both dimensions.

key_moments.label: Small offsets, big change
key_moments.description: The nose side point mainly controls depth, so even small vertical offsets visibly change the profile; align to lower-eyelid height.

key_moments.label: Forehead point at hairline
key_moments.description: Placing the forehead point near the hairline prevents an unnaturally compressed, pulled-back forehead.

key_moments.label: Correct wide-angle distortion
key_moments.description: Face Planar Perspective in the Headshot morph panel compensates for standard/wide-angle lens distortion in the source photo - a likeness fix applied as a morph slider.

key_moments.label: CC5 HD facial profile
key_moments.description: Names the feature as CC5-specific, establishing the CC5 label for expression editing in this video.

key_moments.label: No eyelid/eyeball intersection
key_moments.description: HD profile prevents eyelid-eyeball interpenetration in puppeted expressions - a mesh-penetration fix that is morph-driven, not collision-driven.

key_moments.label: iClone face puppet supports HD
key_moments.description: The HD profile carries over into iClone's face puppet, so the profile is not CC-only.

key_moments.label: Extended profile penetrates
key_moments.description: States the limitation being fixed: Extended profile characters get mesh penetration or distortion when pushed too far.

key_moments.label: Nonlinear lip stickiness
key_moments.description: Lip animation uses a nonlinear lip stickiness effect, also applied to eyebrows - a nonlinear morph behaviour whose survival through export is worth testing.

key_moments.label: MetaHuman-style control panel
key_moments.description: HD face control panel mirrors Unreal/MetaHuman facial controls and exists in both Character Creator and iClone.

key_moments.label: Unreal Control Rig compatible
key_moments.description: Unreal Control Rig and third-party pipelines are fully compatible and can run alongside MetaHuman animation.

key_moments.label: 160 vs 262 morphs
key_moments.description: Hard numbers: Extended profile 160 expression morphs, HD profile 262 total, with 11 eye, 80 mouth and 11 neck sliders added - the morph/shape-key count any export target must carry.

key_moments.label: Corrective morphs introduced
key_moments.description: Corrective sliders automatically fix oddities when multiple morph shapes blend - the corrective layer is driven, not authored.

key_moments.label: 128 corrective morphs
key_moments.description: HD profile ships 128 corrective morphs; whether these export as separate morph targets matters for Blender/GLB transfer.

key_moments.label: Correctives off distorts
key_moments.description: Disabling corrective morphs zeroes them and the combined expressions distort - proves correctives are load-bearing for quality.

key_moments.label: Pout lips now close
key_moments.description: Concrete fix: previous profile left lips partially open on pout; correctives close them.

key_moments.label: Gum exposure compensated
key_moments.description: Old open-mouth shapes exposed too much gum due to excessive strength; correctives compensate automatically.

key_moments.label: Wrinkle folds from mocap
key_moments.description: Strong muscle contractions in mocap now generate natural wrinkle folds - wrinkle detail tied to the HD profile.

key_moments.label: AccuFace benefits too
key_moments.description: HD profile improvements extend from Live Face to AccuFace mocap.

key_moments.label: Nonlinear toggle in Motion LIVE
key_moments.description: Nonlinear behaviour is a recording-time toggle in Motion LIVE, so it is baked into the recorded animation.

key_moments.label: Corrective Expression in Modify
key_moments.description: Corrective expression is a switch in the Modify panel - a per-character setting that must be on for correctives to apply.

key_moments.label: Edits auto-key timeline
key_moments.description: Changing HD face controllers automatically adds a key to the timeline - editing is keyframe-based layering.

key_moments.label: Display Layer Key Value Only
key_moments.description: Unchecking this option previews the full combined result of base animation plus corrected layer keys.

key_moments.label: UE5 skeleton FBX preset
key_moments.description: Export uses FBX with Target Tool Preset Unreal UE5 Skeleton and Export Range All - the stated export recipe for HD facial animation.

key_moments.label: Import Morph Target required
key_moments.description: In Unreal, Import Morph Target must be enabled to bring in the Character Creator morphs; Import Animation with Animated Time carries the curves.

key_moments.label: All morph sliders transferred
key_moments.description: Confirms all expression morph sliders survive the FBX transfer into an Unreal animation sequence - evidence facial animation travels as morph curves.

key_moments.label: Control Rig, Maya, others
key_moments.description: Latest Control Rig fully supports HD facial profile; also compatible with Maya and other third-party pipelines (Blender not named).

key_moments.label: MetaHuman sync deferred
key_moments.description: HD profile characters can sync with MetaHuman and apply its animations - covered in another tutorial.

key_moments.label: Three lash control axes
key_moments.description: The video frames CC5 eyelash quality as three key elements - morphs, materials and positioning - which structure the whole tutorial.

key_moments.label: Why old lashes vanished
key_moments.description: Old eyelashes were single pieces of geometry; from the side the thin geometry is nearly invisible, so lashes disappear at certain camera angles and look flat.

key_moments.label: Stacked mesh pieces
key_moments.description: Wireframe shows upper and lower lashes are several mesh pieces stacked together - lashes are separate geometry (not body mesh), which matters for what an export must carry.

key_moments.label: Lashes follow eye animation
key_moments.description: Narrator claims the new lashes conform realistically to a wide range of eye animations - motion behaviour is built into the lash content, not physics.

key_moments.label: Modular lash parts
key_moments.description: Content ships as full sets plus separate upper lashes, lower lashes and decorative accessories, each with pairing options.

key_moments.label: Replace vs Add apply mode
key_moments.description: Applying lash content offers Replace or Add; Add stacks a new layer on top of existing lashes instead of swapping them.

key_moments.label: Three morph merge options
key_moments.description: Keep Morph, Add Morph and Replace Morph decide how the new lashes' morphs combine with the existing ones; Replace overwrites the original morphs, Keep preserves previous morph settings.

key_moments.label: Scene Manager for lash parts
key_moments.description: Every eyelash component is tracked in the Scene Manager, where hide or delete manages or fixes individual parts - the lash is a multi-object assembly.

key_moments.label: Accessory only allows Add
key_moments.description: With no accessories applied, Add is the only available option; Keep Morph keeps the existing lash shape while attaching the accessory to the lower lashes.

key_moments.label: Add Morph creates sliders
key_moments.description: Stacking with Add Morph (rather than Keep) gives each new layer its own morph slider, enabling per-layer shaping - this is how eyelash morphs are stored per layer.

key_moments.label: Four sliders in current used
key_moments.description: After two upper and two lower layers, four eyelash morph sliders appear under current used; yellow regions indicate the current lash shapes each controls.

key_moments.label: Original sliders still apply
key_moments.description: Per-layer sliders coexist with the original eyelash morph sliders and the Headshot slider, so lash shape is a stack of several morph sources.

key_moments.label: Lashes follow facial morphs
key_moments.description: Facial-structure morphs and eye-size changes keep the lashes on the eyelid contours - lashes are driven by the head's morphs, relevant to whether morph sets export with the lash meshes.

key_moments.label: Lashes use hair shader
key_moments.description: The eyelash material is the Digital Human Hair shader, not a simple opacity card - relevant to whether lash look survives export to other engines (a custom CC shader parameter set; export fidelity is not discussed).

key_moments.label: Root darker, tip lighter
key_moments.description: Stated convention for realistic lashes: end color slightly lighter, root slightly darker; the two can be swapped.

key_moments.label: Specular direction control
key_moments.description: Specular Direction sets the direction and flow of the lash gloss - an anisotropic hair-shader parameter that is unlikely to map 1:1 to a standard glTF PBR material.

key_moments.label: Makeup layer on lashes
key_moments.description: A dedicated makeup section on the lash material gives exaggerated colour and enhanced reflectivity, separate from the base root/end colours.

key_moments.label: Age-appropriate grey lashes
key_moments.description: For elderly characters the narrator recommends a grayish-white lash colour plus specular radiance angle tweaks.

key_moments.label: GoZ mesh-only export
key_moments.description: Because only the shape is edited, only the mesh (no textures) is sent to ZBrush via GoZ - the round trip carries geometry, not materials.

key_moments.label: Lashes left unedited
key_moments.description: Lashes are deliberately not sculpted in ZBrush; the realignment is delegated back to Character Creator's Correct Position.

key_moments.label: Lashes detach after reshaping
key_moments.description: After the GoZ round trip the separate eyelash meshes no longer follow the enlarged eyelids - the lashes are separate geometry that does not automatically re-conform to an externally edited head.

key_moments.label: Disable transparency to inspect
key_moments.description: Turning off eyelash transparency is the stated way to see the lash mesh deviating from the eye mesh it was attached to.

key_moments.label: Correct Position auto-realigns
key_moments.description: Character > Correct Position automatically realigns the lashes, optionally per selected part - the fix for any head-shape change.

key_moments.label: Full is default, may distort
key_moments.description: Default positioning is Full, which moves the whole lash mesh but may slightly alter the overall lash shape.

key_moments.label: Root preserves lash shape
key_moments.description: Root keeps the original lash shape and only stretches the base to the new eyelid contour; the difference grows with larger shape changes (459s).

key_moments.label: Lashes corrected per expression
key_moments.description: Correct Position also works inside Edit Expression mode, so lash behaviour on blink is stored per expression - lashes ride facial morphs rather than bones.

key_moments.label: Update writes to morph slider
key_moments.description: Clicking Update saves the corrected lash angle into the expression morph slider itself - the lash correction becomes part of the morph data, which is what would need to survive an FBX/GLB morph export.

key_moments.label: Each side corrected separately
key_moments.description: The blink correction must be repeated for the opposite eye's lashes using the parts and angle settings.

key_moments.label: Set Custom Position state
key_moments.description: Set Custom Position saves the current lash placement as a custom state and activates the Custom option, so a hand-tuned placement can be the reference for later corrections.

key_moments.label: Repeat GoZ breaks alignment
key_moments.description: Every further GoZ reshape knocks the lashes out of alignment again; Correct Position with Root is the recommended re-fix.

key_moments.label: CC5 pack ships HD eyes
key_moments.description: Establishes the app as CC5: the CC5 character pack provides the HD eye library, so these assets and shaders are CC5-specific.

key_moments.label: Replace completely vs material
key_moments.description: Applying an eye prompts Replace Completely or Material Only; Material Only changes colour without swapping the eye mesh - relevant to keeping mesh/rig intact for export.

key_moments.label: 2K scanned iris textures
key_moments.description: HD eye materials move from legacy 1K to 2K textures scanned from real eyeballs - a texture-budget number to account for in GLB size.

key_moments.label: Iris depth is refraction
key_moments.description: Iris Depth Scale works by controlling lighting refraction; refraction is a shader effect that standard glTF PBR does not carry, so it likely must be faked or baked downstream.

key_moments.label: Limbus enlarges iris
key_moments.description: Limbus Dark Scale and Width Color increase apparent iris size and shading without a geometry change.

key_moments.label: Sclera flatten normal
key_moments.description: The normal map in the Texture section plus Sclera Flatten Normal controls blood-vessel relief - a normal-map-driven detail that does travel as a standard map.

key_moments.label: Eyelid shadow controls
key_moments.description: Shadow intensity, range and tint fake eyelid shadowing on the eyeball inside the shader - another CC-only parameter set.

key_moments.label: Occlusion and tearline are HD
key_moments.description: Both eye occlusion and tearline shaders carry the HD suffix: these are separate eye elements with their own shaders, not part of the eyeball material.

key_moments.label: Use Display Blur Range
key_moments.description: Explicit recommendation: enable Display Blur Range while adjusting occlusion, because with it disabled the effect and its range are hard to inspect.

key_moments.label: Tearline wetness via roughness
key_moments.description: Tearline wetness is controlled by roughness, with tiling and micronormal for surface detail.

key_moments.label: Elements can be repositioned
key_moments.description: Eye occlusion and tearline elements can be repositioned - they are separate meshes that must stay aligned to the eyelids through any transfer.

key_moments.label: Purpose of Extended Plus
key_moments.description: States the profile's goal: more vivid lip detail, improved nonlinear facial performance and precise lip sync for mocap-driven talking animation.

key_moments.label: Starting point: CC4 Extended
key_moments.description: The base profile is named the 'CC4 extended profile'; Extended Plus is an upgrade of it, not a separate rig, which matters for compatibility with existing CC4 characters and exports.

key_moments.label: Corrective toggle is the upgrade
key_moments.description: A single Corrective option converts CC4 Extended to Extended Plus - the whole upgrade is gated on one switch in Edit Expression.

key_moments.label: Save-previous-settings choice
key_moments.description: Upgrading offers to keep the previous profile settings; declining it (as shown) means the old profile state is not preserved, a one-way gotcha worth knowing before upgrading.

key_moments.label: Why correctives exist
key_moments.description: Corrective shapes automatically fix oddities that occur when multiple morph shapes blend - the core argument for combination correctives over additive morphs.

key_moments.label: Disabling correctives distorts
key_moments.description: Turning corrective morphs off resets the corrective sliders to zero and the morph combinations over-add and distort - so an export that drops correctives will look worse than the CC viewport.

key_moments.label: Correctives are driven automatically
key_moments.description: Corrective slider strengths follow the expression slider strength automatically; they are driven values, which is the key question for any transfer that only carries raw shape keys (Blender/GLB).

key_moments.label: 68 corrective sliders
key_moments.description: The profile adds 68 corrective sliders across regions, concentrated in the mouth - the morph count to expect on export.

key_moments.label: Pucker lip closure fix
key_moments.description: Without correctives the lips cannot fully close on Pucker; correctives resolve it - a concrete lip-sync quality gain.

key_moments.label: Gum exposure fix
key_moments.description: Without correctives the gums are overly exposed on mouth open; with them the shape is natural.

key_moments.label: iPhone or AccuFACE mocap
key_moments.description: Claims a full facial mocap quality upgrade with responsive nonlinear talking animation for both iPhone and AccuFACE (caption reads 'Acuase').

key_moments.label: 26 nonlinear mouth sliders
key_moments.description: Enabling correctives populates the Custom section with 26 sliders dedicated to nonlinear mouth morphs - a second morph block on top of the 68 correctives.

key_moments.label: Sticky lips on streaming mocap
key_moments.description: The nonlinear sliders give a sticky-lips effect while streaming mocap, improving lip connection - the headline nonlinear feature.

key_moments.label: Nonlinear curve easing
key_moments.description: A nonlinear curve slider applies ease in / ease out to lip animation - shaping applied at the profile level, not keyframe tangents.

key_moments.label: Motion Live nonlinear toggle
key_moments.description: Motion Live exposes a nonlinear toggle during recording, so the nonlinear effect is applied at capture time and baked into the recorded clip.

key_moments.label: Modify panel corrective toggle
key_moments.description: Corrective Expression can also be switched in the Modify panel for before/after comparison - a second place the setting lives.

key_moments.label: Unreal UE5 skeleton preset
key_moments.description: Export FBX uses Target Tool Preset 'Unreal UE5 skeleton' with Export Range All - the stated export recipe for the Extended Plus animation.

key_moments.label: Import Morph Targets required
key_moments.description: In Unreal, Import Morph Targets must be enabled or the morph data (including correctives) is not included; Import Animation on with Animation Length = Animated Time.

key_moments.label: Morphs survive to Unreal
key_moments.description: Opening the animation sequence confirms all morphs are correctly applied - evidence that Extended Plus morph animation survives FBX transfer as morph-target curves.

key_moments.label: Updated control rig support
key_moments.description: The updated (Unreal) control rig can take advantage of the Extended Plus profile, so it is not only baked playback.

key_moments.label: Other pipelines claimed
key_moments.description: Narrator says Extended Plus animation brings realism to other pipelines and transfers smoothly across workflows; the description names Unreal, Maya and other third-party apps but Blender/GLB is never shown.
